blocks.html: Services are bought, not sold. That's the philosophy behind how we work a deal at OneAccord. Your job isn't to push a prospect through a pipeline — it's to help them move through their own buying journey, at their own pace, by earning each step honestly. That's exactly what the Buyer's Journey module (what you'd call "Opportunities" or "Deals" in a lot of other CRMs) is built to track.

1. What is a Buyer's Journey Record?

A Buyer's Journey record represents a potential piece of business.

  • It is always linked to a Contact (the person) and a Company.
  • It has a specific dollar value and an estimated closing date.

2. The B.U.Y.E.R.S. Framework

Every stage in the pipeline is named for what the prospect has to do — not what you, the rep, believe or hope is true. Each stage requires both conditions below before you move forward:

  • Bothered: The prospect can identify the problem, and can articulate a real sense of urgency.
  • Understand: The prospect can articulate the scope of the problem and their desired outcome, and they inquire how to achieve those objectives.
  • Yearning: The prospect explicitly states their desire — e.g., "This is what I need" — and can describe the approach in their own words.
  • Explainable: The prospect can explain the value in their own words, and can defend the decision to their own stakeholders.
  • Ready: The prospect gives a specific verbal commitment — e.g., "I'm in!" — and confirms final approval.
  • Started: The prospect signs the contract, and submits payment, and commits resources.
  • Finished: The deal is Closed Won and the engagement itself has been delivered — this is the true finish line, not just the signature.

Eight rules underpin all of it: Don't skip steps. No urgency = no opportunity. To yearn, they must understand. Yearning must be verbal and mutual. Buyers must be able to justify their decision. Enthusiasm ≠ commitment. If it isn't paid for, it isn't a deal yet. Celebrate the chance to deliver value.

3. Moving Through the Pipeline (The Blue Boxes)

At OneAccord, we don't just "drag and drop" a record forward. We use Blueprints — the colored transition buttons at the top of a Leads or Buyer's Journey record. They act as a guided path, showing you exactly what the next step is.

  • Linear Progress: You must click these buttons to advance the stage.
  • Locked Fields: You may notice the "Stage" field is locked — this is intentional! The Blueprint ensures we follow our standardized process and don't skip a step.

4. Prove It, Don't Assume It

Because every stage depends on the prospect's own words, not your read of the room, we need real evidence behind every stage move — not a rep's best guess that "they seemed pretty into it."

  • Record your calls in Microsoft Teams. The transcript lives there afterward, so you can go back and find the prospect's exact words — the actual quote that shows they've reached "This is what I need" or "I'm in," not just your paraphrase of it.
  • The automated call-notes email. Once this rolls out, you'll get an automated email after your call with notes and a suggested Buyer's Journey stage, formatted so you can copy the relevant language straight into Zoho. It's a shortcut for documentation — you still have to click the Blueprint button yourself to actually move the stage.

5. Stage Corrections

We are all human! If you accidentally move a record to the wrong stage, look for a transition button labeled "Correction - [stage name]" (e.g., "Correction - Bothered"). This allows you to fix the error without the record getting stuck.

6. Automation & Notifications

Our pipeline has "eyes." You may see automations in Zoho reminding you to take action on a record — these exist to make sure nothing goes stale. A record's "Last Update" timestamp is a quick visual cue too: if it's been a while, that's your signal to go get the next real signal from the prospect, not to just click the button anyway.

blocks.prompt: According to the B.U.Y.E.R.S. framework, what must happen before you move a record from "Understand" to "Yearning"?
options: 30 days must pass in the current stage
The prospect must explicitly state their desire in their own words, and be able to describe the approach themselves
The rep decides the prospect seems interested enough
A Managing Principal must sign off
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the prospect has to explicitly state their desire ("This is what I need") and describe the approach in their own words before you move to Yearning.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Not quite — the prospect must explicitly state their desire in their own words and be able to describe the approach themselves. It's their words that move the stage, not your read of the room.

blocks.prompt: True or False: If a prospect seems excited and enthusiastic about your proposal, that's enough to move the record to "Ready."
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right — enthusiasm isn't commitment. "Ready" requires a specific verbal commitment ("I'm in!") plus confirmed final approval.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: False — enthusiasm isn't commitment. "Ready" requires a specific verbal commitment ("I'm in!") plus confirmed final approval, not just good vibes on the call.

blocks.prompt: Where should you find the exact words a prospect used to justify moving a record forward?
options: Your own notes summarizing the gist of the call
The Teams recording/transcript of your call, or the automated call-notes email once it's live
Zia's Best Time to Contact suggestion
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the Teams transcript (and eventually the automated call-notes email) is where you find the prospect's actual words, not your summary of them.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: You'd look at the Teams recording/transcript of your call, or the automated call-notes email once it's live — you need their actual words, not your paraphrase.
